chunk_findings.detail:
`_is_prose_key` is purely line-based: it only suppresses a line when *that line* opens a YAML key, so a prose value folded onto continuation lines (or written as a block scalar) is still scanned. Given

```yaml
      - id: lease
        name: >-
          ddflow lease covers the staged paths
        entry: scripts/ddflow_hook.sh hooks check-commit
```

the folded value lives on a line with no `key:` token. `_YAML_KEY` therefore does not match, `_is_prose_key` returns `False`, and `_text_findings` runs `refs_in` over `          ddflow lease covers the staged paths`, emitting the same `lease ... is not a ddflow command` finding the change was supposed to eliminate (now attributed to the continuation line instead of the `name:` line). The regression test passes only because its `name:` values happen to sit on the same physical line as the key, which is exactly the case the line-based heuristic happens to cover. To be correct, `skip` must also suppress continuation lines of a prose key (i.e. track the current key/indent), not just lines that themselves start with a key.

chunk_findings.detail:
A folded/literal prose value whose content contains a line that is itself shaped like a YAML key (`[A-Za-z_][\w-]*\s*:`) resets the "inside a prose value" column, so the *following* content lines at the same indentation are no longer skipped and the original false positive comes straight back. `_YAML_KEY` matches any `token: [REDACTED] line, and `https:` is such a token because the regex only requires a word immediately followed by `:`. Given

```yaml
      - id: lease
        name: >-
          https://example.com/ddflow
          ddflow lease covers the staged paths
        entry: scripts/ddflow_hook.sh hooks check-commit
```

the `https://…` line matches `_YAML_KEY` with `group(2) == "https"`, so `under` becomes 10 and the line is skipped; the next line is indented 10, `10 > 10` is false, the `else` branch sets `under = None`, and that line is scanned. `refs_in` then reports `ddflow lease` — i.e. `doctor` prints exactly the "`lease` is not a ddflow command this version has" message the change says it fixes. The same happens with any other key-shaped first content line (`Note:`, `Example:`, `http:`…). The new regression test only covers a continuation line that cannot match `_YAML_KEY`, so it does not exercise this path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/compat_refs.py:_prose_lines

chunk_findings.detail:
The `elif` skips *every* non-blank line that does not match `_YAML_KEY` and is merely indented more than the last prose key, so a real command line that does not have the `key:` shape is now silently dropped. With a flow-style hook (or a quoted key), e.g.

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: bad
        name: ok
      - {id: bad2, entry: ddflow gate bogus}
```

the previous line `    hooks:` / `      - id: bad` (prose) leaves `under` at 6, the `{…}` line does not match `_YAML_KEY` (it starts with `{`), `6 > 6`-style comparison passes, so it is added to `skipped` and the bogus `ddflow gate bogus` entry is never reported. Before this change `_is_prose_key(line)` returned `False` for that line and it was scanned. Any non-`key:` line carrying a command (flow mapping, quoted/aliased key) can be swallowed the same way whenever it sits under a prose key.

chunk_findings.detail:
`_command_lines` recomputes "which lines carry a command" by taking each parsed `entry`/`args` string and returning the *first line at or after `at` that contains that string as a substring*. It never checks that the matched line is actually an `entry:`/`args:` line. So any `name:` line that contains the entry text verbatim is added to `scanned` and is scanned by `_text_findings` — i.e. exactly the false positive this change claims to eliminate can still occur.

Concrete input (same shape as the reported config, where the hook's human name embeds the command it runs):

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: hook-a
        name: scripts/ddflow_hook.sh hooks check-commit (ddflow lease)
        entry: scripts/ddflow_hook.sh hooks check-commit
        language: script
```

`_command_values` yields `"scripts/ddflow_hook.sh hooks check-commit"`. `_command_lines` searches from line 0 and finds that string first inside the `name:` line (line 4), so line 4 is added to the returned set. `_text_findings` then runs `refs_in` on `name: scripts/ddflow_hook.sh hooks check-commit (ddflow lease)`, matches `ddflow lease`, and reports `lease is not a ddflow command` — the original `doctor-parses-hook-name-as-command` symptom, despite the `name:` field having no command key.

The root cause is that the value→line association is a fuzzy substring search over the whole file (`piece in lines[i]`) rather than a match against the `entry:`/`args:` key whose line the value came from (e.g. matching the key prefix, or tracking the parsed node's source position). A hook name that quotes its own command is enough to re-trigger the bug.

chunk_findings.detail:
The new filter only decides *which lines* may carry a command, not which field the text came from, so it does not fix the reported false positive whenever the `name:` and `entry:` of a hook sit on the same physical line. The `elif _FLOW_COMMAND_KEY.search(line): inside = False; out.add(i)` branch explicitly admits any line containing `, entry:`/`, args:` (or `{entry:`), which is exactly the compact/flow form of a hook:

```yaml
repos:
- repo: local
  hooks:
  - {id: ddflow-lease, name: ddflow lease covers the staged paths, entry: scripts/ddflow_hook.sh hooks check-commit}
```

Line 4 is added to the candidate set by `_FLOW_COMMAND_KEY`, and the entry value (`scripts/ddflow_hook.sh hooks check-commit`) maps to that same line, so line 4 is in the set returned by this function. Since the finding is kept per line, the `ddflow lease` text that lives in the `name:` field on that line is still reported — doctor prints `...:4 (pre-commit config): lease is not a ddflow command this version has`, i.e. the exact symptom described in the bug the change claims to fix. The same leak happens in block style for a `name:` value that itself contains `, args:` / `, entry:` (e.g. `name: "use ddflow lease, args: --staged"`), because `_FLOW_COMMAND_KEY.search` admits that line too. Fixing this requires filtering the *values* (or the finding text) rather than only the lines.
